primitives.note: Udyr has no ultimate; Q/W/E/R are each a Stance he swaps into, each empowering his next two basic attacks differently and overriding the previous stance's unused empowered attacks; switching stances does not end effects the previous stance already granted.

Every stance cast (and its Awaken recast) arms Udyr's next two on-hit basic attacks with the stance's bonus effect (Q: physical on-hit + AS; W: lifesteal+heal+shield; E: dash-stun; R: AoE magic pulse).

Each stance has an 'Awaken' recast (0.25-5s after the initial cast) that adds a stronger secondary effect (Q: lightning chain; W: bigger shield + HoT + doubled lifesteal/heal; E: bonus speed + CC immunity; R: storm becomes a mobile pulsing zone with % max-health damage) and refreshes/consumes the ability's cooldown.

Monk Training: after casting any basic ability, Udyr's next two on-hit basic attacks gain 30% bonus attack speed for 4s, independent of and stacking with the active stance's own empowered-attack effect.

A 1.5s global cooldown is incurred on Q/W/E/R whenever one of them is cast; Monk Training refunds 5% of Awakened Spirit's total cooldown per proc (unless <1s remaining); Awaken recasts refresh (do not simply continue) the stance ability's 6s cooldown.
Mana costs (Q flat 20; W/E/R 40 scaling down by champion level per wiki, flat 40 per bin) on 6s-cooldown abilities can matter over a 15s fight with heavy stance-cycling.
Storm Stance's blizzard deals magic damage every 0.5s for 4s around Udyr (and, after Awaken, from a separately-moving unleashed storm).
Q's on-hit bonus damage, Awaken bonus damage and lightning strikes, and R's blizzard/storm/pulse damage are all expressed partly as a percentage of the target's maximum health.
Q grants a stacking-capable bonus attack speed buff for 4s (base + Awaken addition); W's empowered attacks grant lifesteal (doubled on Awaken) that persists as a buff until two attacks land.
R's Awaken recast detaches the storm into an independently-moving unit that seeks out and follows the target, dealing its own damage over time separate from Udyr's attacks/position.

needsBespoke.why: Udyr's kit layers mechanics no single primitive (or simple combination) cleanly captures: (1) four interchangeable 'ultimate-like' abilities sharing one passive 'Awakened Spirit' charge with its own long, level/ultimate-haste-scaled cooldown (~50s to 20s) that is separate from each ability's own 6s cooldown and must be spent via a precisely-timed 0.25-5s recast window after entering a stance; (2) a 1.5s shared global cooldown across all four abilities layered on top of their individual cooldowns; (3) Monk Training's onhit-rider stacking with whichever stance's own empowered-attack effect is simultaneously active, including special-cased reactivation on Awaken casts that also re-applies the stance's un-awakened attack effect. Modeling how much of this fits in a single 15s fight (especially whether even one Awaken is achievable) needs bespoke sequencing logic beyond composing the closed-list primitives.

proposal: Open by casting Q (Wilding Claw) to enter Claw Stance, arming the next two basic attacks and starting the attack-speed buff.
Auto-attack immediately and continuously; the two empowered attacks trigger Q's bonus on-hit physical damage.

Within 0.25-5s of the Q cast, if Awakened Spirit is available, recast Q to Awaken it, gaining the lightning-chain empowered attacks and extra attack speed; keep auto-attacking to land all lightning ticks on the dummy.
Respect the shared 1.5s global cooldown before casting any other stance ability after Q.

Recast Q again as soon as its 6s cooldown is up to refresh Claw Stance and repeat the empowered on-hit damage, since Q has the lowest cost/cooldown and the most direct offensive on-hit and health%-based damage of the four stances.
Weave in R (Wingborne Storm) once per its 6s cooldown when it does not delay a Q recast, for its self-centered blizzard DoT and its own empowered on-hit pulse damage against the stationary dummy.

Do not prioritize W (Iron Mantle) for damage output, since it grants only self-healing/shielding/lifesteal with no offensive on-hit component, which the damage-only dummy fight does not need; only cast it if mana/cooldown are otherwise idle and lifesteal-on-hit itemization needs to be exercised.

Do not prioritize E (Blazing Stampede) beyond triggering it to keep attacking; its offensive contribution is limited to a CC stun (ignored per instructions) and movement speed (ignored), so it contributes no ranked damage benefit versus a stationary dummy.
Keep basic-attacking without gaps throughout the 15s window so Monk Training's post-cast attack-speed buff is never wasted.
questions: Given Awakened Spirit's long level/ultimate-haste-scaled cooldown (~20-50s), how many Awaken casts, if any, should the simulator assume occur within a single 15s fight, and does that make W/E irrelevant to include in the rotation at all?
Should the simulator assume perfect execution of the 0.25-5s Awaken recast timing every time it's available, or apply a realistic reaction delay that could cause the window to be missed?

Is it correct to fully skip W and E in the damage-maximizing rotation, or does casting them still contribute indirectly (e.g., via Monk Training's attack-speed proc) enough to be worth weaving in over just spamming Q and R?
